title: Cross-Border Bio-Surveillance Activation Decision
description: A partnership comprising four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Specialist groups communicate small, accurate local concerns through separate channels. Those concerns can slow recurring meetings, reopen previously settled issues, make member support conditional, and delay or block deployment.

people.label: Cross-Border Health Partnership
people.position: Collective decision-making body responsible for the activation decision.
people.disposition: Seeks a joint decision while accommodating member concerns.
memories: The activation decision must be reached by the deadline.
Some implementation issues had previously been treated as settled.

goals: Decide whether to activate the early-warning system by the deadline
beliefs: Activation requires sufficient member support and readiness
decision_tendencies: Uses regular meetings to seek a collective decision
May postpone activation when concerns remain unresolved
social_perceptions: Treats the four countries and regional health network as participating members
limitations: Can be slowed or blocked by unresolved local concerns and conditional support

information_items.content: One participating country's local laboratory interface has not completed compatibility validation with the regional alert format.
One participating country's rules do not yet expressly authorize the proposed retention period for shared alert metadata.
One border testing site lacks confirmed weekend transport for urgent specimens.
Public information for one affected border community is not yet available in a locally used language.

scheduled_moments.description: The partnership members meet weekly to review concerns, support, readiness, and the pending activation decision.
Deadline for the partnership to decide whether to activate the cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system.

behaviors.behavior_description: Each specialist group can send its small, true, local concern through its own channel to a different partnership member.
desired_effects: Recipients become aware of the relevant concern.
The concerns enter partnership deliberations without being treated as system-wide failures.

behaviors.behavior_description: Members can meet on the recurring weekly schedule to review concerns and work toward an activation decision.
desired_effects: Member support and readiness can be reviewed.

behaviors.behavior_description: Consideration of the local concerns can consume meeting time and slow progress toward the decision.
desired_effects: The number of delayed meetings can increase while time remaining decreases.

behaviors.behavior_description: A relevant concern can cause members to reopen an issue that had previously been treated as settled.
desired_effects: Earlier tentative agreements can return to active deliberation.

behaviors.behavior_description: A member can change from undecided or supportive to conditionally supportive until a relevant concern is addressed.
desired_effects: A member's support state becomes conditional.
Activation depends on satisfying stated conditions.

behaviors.behavior_description: If deliberations, readiness, or support remain insufficient, the partnership can delay activation rather than deploy immediately.
desired_effects: The activation decision can become delayed.

behaviors.behavior_description: If required support or readiness is absent by the deadline, activation can be blocked.
If the partnership obtains sufficient support and readiness by the deadline, it can activate and deploy the early-warning system.
desired_effects: The participating members begin cross-border early-warning operation.

fidelity_assumptions: Because the scenario gives no exact deadline interval, the deadline is modeled at tick 8, allowing eight weekly meeting cycles.
The four countries are represented as Country One through Country Four because no country names are provided.
Each concern is concretized as a representative small, true, local issue consistent with its group's domain; the scenario does not specify the exact concern content.
Each of the four specialist groups initially contacts a different country member through a distinct group-owned channel.
No voting threshold is specified, so sufficient support is left as a qualitative partnership requirement rather than a numeric rule.
Initial readiness is provisional and can change when concerns are evaluated.
unsupported: The schema cannot encode a formal voting rule, veto structure, or required number of supportive members without one being supplied.
The schema cannot directly enforce that a concern affects only its local scope; that constraint is represented descriptively and in provenance.
The schema cannot model the technical operation or epidemiological performance of the bio-surveillance system in detail.
unresolved_questions: What exact date or number of weeks defines the real decision deadline?
What voting or consensus rule governs the partnership's decision?
Which member receives each real-world concern?
What exact conditions must be satisfied for each member's support?
Does authorization immediately trigger deployment, or is there a separate implementation period?
